observations: A large rounded head fills most of the canvas, built from dense overlapping scribble lines in dark brown and black, with patches of yellow, teal, and purple breaking across the forehead and cheeks.

The eyes are asymmetric: the left socket is heavily shadowed with deep black hatching and a small green highlight; the right sits higher, ringed in black with a pale white surround, giving the face an off-balance look.

Around the head, loose strokes of red, blue, yellow, and green extend to the black edges—vertical blue bars on the right, red scrawls top and bottom-left—keeping the background active without forming recognizable shapes.
reading: The face pushes close to the picture edge, leaving little breathing room. Dense scribble lines pile up around the eyes and mouth, where a gap of white teeth and a red interior sit below a clenched jaw. The surrounding color bursts feel separate from the face—raw and unresolved rather than decorative. The asymmetric eyes pull the reading off-center, suggesting unease without naming it.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between nnxyz nnotb #259 and nnxyz nnotb #261 in both title and recorded-creation order. Where #259 spreads its face across a saturated yellow field with open line work, #260 compresses into a darker, more enclosed space.

connections.reason: Both works center a face with mismatched eye treatments and an open mouth showing teeth, but #259 uses a bright yellow ground with loose outlines while #260 builds the same structure in darker, denser hatching—a direct tonal contrast between neighbors.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly does the scribble line work end and the background color strokes begin—and does that boundary hold consistently around the whole head?
ambiguities: The pale strip at the very top of the head reads as either a highlight or an unpainted gap; the image does not resolve which.
